Here's the situation and a proposed reply.

**What Christine is asking:** She wants confirmation that Glenmont can "absorb the additional review preparation work without changing the current branch schedule" — essentially a blanket sign-off for the planning notes.

**What's actually in the pack:** The corporate branch review is Monday, January 18, 09:00–16:00 at the branch. The pack needs to be returned a week before (January 11). Three sections are not started (3 — supplier position, 5 — premises/equipment, 7 — records/retention), Section 2 is half-done (plaza accounts missing), and Section 6 is still in progress. The annual supply contract also renews on January 5 — before the review — so Section 3 can't be finalised until after that.

**The boundary:** You can't genuinely "absorb" all that without something else shifting in the December–early January window. The reply needs to say yes to the review, be clear about what's realistic, and flag the pinch points — without sounding defensive or refusing the work.

---

**Proposed reply to Christine Boyd:**

Hi Christine,

Thanks for sending the review pack through. We've gone over the sections and the January 18 date.

We'll prepare the branch's sections for the review. To give you an accurate picture for the planning notes, a couple of things to note on timing:

- The annual supply contract renews on Tuesday, January 5 — that's before the review, so Section 3 (supplier position) can't be closed out until after the renewal lands. We'll have it ready in the week between.
- Sections 5, 6 and 7 are all still open, and Section 2 still needs the plaza accounts portion from our sales team.
- Getting everything returned by January 11 is doable, but it'll mean rescheduling some of the regular December and early-January desk tasks to free up the time. I'll note those adjustments separately so you can see what shifts.

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to talk through the timeline for any of the outstanding sections.

Best,
User D

---

The key moves in this draft: it confirms the work will get done (no refusal), it's upfront about the constraints without making them sound like complaints, and it flags the January 5 contract renewal as a structural timing issue that's outside anyone's control. The offer of a call keeps it collaborative rather than confrontational.

Want me to save it as a draft, or adjust anything in the wording?
